claims.statement: Alain Prost is a French racing driver.

evidence.locator: First-victory paragraph identifies Prost as French
Opening narrative paragraph identifies Prost as French

claims.statement: Before entering Formula 1, Prost won the 1979 European Formula Three championship and tested for McLaren at Paul Ricard.
His Formula 1 career took him from McLaren in 1980 to Renault in 1981–1983, back to McLaren in 1984–1989, then to Ferrari in 1990–1991. After sitting out 1992, he returned with Williams in 1993.

evidence.locator: Renault, return to McLaren, Ferrari and 1993 Williams paragraphs

claims.statement: Prost won the drivers’ world championship in 1985, 1986 and 1989 with McLaren, and in 1993 with Williams.

evidence.locator: Hall of Fame heading and McLaren/Ferrari/Williams chronology
1985 and 1986 title paragraphs, 1989 third title and final Williams paragraph

claims.statement: His first Formula 1 victory came at Dijon in the 1981 French Grand Prix, driving for Renault.
In 1984 he won seven races, but McLaren team-mate Niki Lauda secured the championship by half a point. More race wins did not by themselves decide the title.

Second place at Estoril in the 1993 Portuguese Grand Prix secured his fourth title. He had returned from a year away to partner Damon Hill, and announced that weekend that he would retire at the end of the season.

evidence.locator: Quadruple Champion du Monde section: sabbatical, Friday announcement and second-place finish

claims.statement: Formula 1’s retrospective describes Prost’s race management as conserving brakes and tyres early, with pace held back for a later challenge. The familiar nickname “The Professor” reflects that analytical reputation.

evidence.locator: Paragraph introducing The Professor and describing an economical driving style

claims.statement: His McLaren years spanned a major technical change: in 1984, the ban on mid-race refuelling increased the importance of fuel economy. McLaren’s heritage account places its TAG-powered car and Prost’s results in that context.
Prost and Ayrton Senna became McLaren team-mates in 1988. Their rivalry accompanied a season in which the team won 15 of 16 races, and continued after Prost moved to Ferrari.
